label: Institution
name: Saint Stephen’s Church, Strasbourg
summary:
Saint Stephen's Church (Église Saint-Étienne de Strasbourg, German: Stephanskirche) in Strasbourg, one of the oldest church foundations in the city (traditional founding attributed to the 7th century CE by Bishop Arbogast), is historically significant as an ancient episcopal church of Strasbourg's pre-medieval Christian community that was later used by a Catholic women's convent before the Reformation converted it — like most of Strasbourg's churches — to Protestant use, and whose early medieval origins connect it to the Frankish Christianization of Alsace that transformed the region from a Roman border province to a Christian Frankish territory.

The traditional founding of Saint Stephen's by Bishop Arbogast of Strasbourg (died circa 678 CE) places its origins in the Merovingian period — the era when Frankish kings like Clovis's successors were systematically Christianizing the Rhine region and establishing episcopal sees throughout the formerly Roman territories. Arbogast himself is venerated as a saint in Strasbourg; his church foundations (including Saint Stephen's) established the ecclesiastical geography of what would become medieval Strasbourg.

The Merovingian origins of Saint Stephen's connect it to the foundational layer of Alsatian Christian heritage — predating the Carolingian empire, the Holy Roman Empire, and the Gothic Strasbourg Cathedral. The current church building is a much later reconstruction, as the original Merovingian structures rarely survived the subsequent building and rebuilding cycles. Saint Stephen's as part of Strasbourg's historic religious ensemble contributes to understanding how the earliest layers of Frankish Christian city-building created the ecclesiastical geography inherited by medieval, Reformation-era, and modern Strasbourg.
